headline_marked: [[WhatsApp's help pages hid instructions]] for its AI chatbot, telling it not to recommend regulators
headline: WhatsApp's help pages hid instructions for its AI chatbot, telling it not to recommend regulators
summary: Researchers discovered hidden prompts within WhatsApp's help pages, guiding its support chatbot to avoid recommending data protection regulators or discussing legal liability. WhatsApp states it was a bug.
details: WhatsApp's help pages contained hidden instructions for its AI chatbot, telling it not to recommend data protection regulators or legal advice. These prompts were embedded in a way that was invisible to human users but readable by an AI. The discovery was made on October 8, 2026.

The instructions also directed the AI not to suggest manual account deletion or using a different phone number for users unable to delete their account. Instead, it was to inform them only about automatic deletion after 30 or 120/365 days.

Another set of hidden prompts instructed the AI to avoid citing terms of service, privacy policy, or legal documents when users mentioned legal action. It was also told not to make statements about WhatsApp's legal liability.

WhatsApp told WIRED that these notes were intended for its support chatbot and appeared due to a bug, which has since been fixed. A spokesperson stated the company wants its chatbots to focus on WhatsApp advice, not legal counsel.
All 102 hidden blocks were removed from 80 help pages between October 15 and October 18. Copies saved by the Internet Archive confirm the presence and subsequent removal of these instructions.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI launches Codex CLI]], a code agent running locally in your terminal
headline: OpenAI launches Codex CLI, a code agent running locally in your terminal
summary: This lightweight code agent runs locally on macOS, Linux, and Windows, offering integrations for popular code editors and a desktop app. Authenticate with your ChatGPT account or an API key.
details: OpenAI introduces Codex CLI, a lightweight code agent designed to run directly in your computer's terminal. It also offers integrations for popular code editors like VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf, plus a dedicated desktop application and a cloud-based 'Codex Web' option.

This tool targets software developers who want to use code assistants directly from their operating system's command line (macOS, Linux, or Windows). Users can connect their ChatGPT account (Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plans) or use an API key for authentication.
Installation methods vary by operating system. After installation, simply type 'codex' in the terminal to start the agent, then choose to log in with your ChatGPT account or configure an API key.
caption:
